title: Value objects through storage and back
pins: The stored form of every text-capability value object, and — where an implementation can rebuild them — that serialising, rebuilding and re-serialising returns the identical bytes. This is the surface an application persists a conversation on, and it is where absent-versus-null, enums and empty maps all bite at once.

php.gap: The reference asserts the SERIALISED half only. particle-academy/prism has no fromArray() for messages — it can write its value objects and cannot read them back — so the rehydration half of every row here is unverified in PHP. That gap is not academic: it forced prism-harness to invent its own MessageMapper, which then shipped a defect that corrupted every stored Anthropic assistant message. See finding F-4.
php.cause_note: The reference has no fromArray() for messages: it can WRITE its value objects and cannot READ THEM BACK, so only the serialised half is asserted. Both ports round-trip.

ts.gap: rtp-0009 is skipped: the reference renders an empty map-typed field as an empty JSON array, which this language cannot express without modelling maps as arrays. See finding F-3.
ts.cause_note: F-3, the same empty-map ambiguity, on rtp-0009.
